newsitem.title: USA: U.S. securities industry posts record Q4 revs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. securities industry posts record Q4 revs.

text.p: The U.S. securities industry posted record fourth quarter revenues of $31.4 billion, surpassing the previous record of $30.5 billion in the second quarter, according to the Securities Industry Association.
The trade group said that total 1996 pre-tax net income for the industry reached $11.27 billion, 31 percent over the previous record of $8.6 billion in 1993.
The SIA said that industry employment reached 265,000 at the end of 1996, which was up 3.5 percent over 1995.
The SIA said securities firms raised more than $1 trillion in capital, with total corporate underwriting alone hitting $954 million.
Merger and acquisition activity also reached record levels, with more than than $500 billion in completed deals in 1996 and initial public offerings raised $50 billion during the year, the SIA said.
"Companies took advantage of the relatively low cost of capital in 1996 to expand," said Jeffrey Schaefer, SIA senior vice president and director of research.

Average daily volume on each of the three major exchanges set records, according to the SIA. The New York Stock Exchange posted 412 million shares daily, up 19 percent over 1995; Nasdaq rose to 544 million shares, up 36 percent; and the American Stock Exchange rose 10 percent to 22 million shares.
